summary: The Nigeria LNG (NLNG) Undergraduate Scholarship Scheme gives a yearly grant, for the whole length of the course, to first-year students at Nigerian federal and state universities. It has run nationally since 2003 and over 3,400 students have benefited. Winners have strong O'Level and UTME results, apply with clean documents, and score well in an online proctored selection test.
lookfor: Five O'Level credits including English and Mathematics in one sitting
Complete, matching documents (WAEC/NECO, JAMB result and admission letter, LGA letter, birth certificate)
Performance in the computer-based online proctored selection test
Final document check for those who pass the test
cycle: The 2025/26 round opened 18 Nov 2025 and closed 12 Dec 2025, for students in their first year in 2025/26. If the pattern holds, the round for 2026/27 first-year students would open around November-December 2026 - check the current guidance and NLNG's official channels.

eligibility.q: Are you a Nigerian citizen living in Nigeria?
eligibility.no: This scheme is only for Nigerians resident in Nigeria. Look for scholarships in your own country.

eligibility.q: Are you a full-time first-year student at a federal or state university in the current session?
eligibility.no: Private-university students and students above 100 level did not qualify in 2025/26. Second-years can look at NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS; medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and engineering students at the Agbami scheme.

eligibility.q: Do you have five O'Level credits, including English and Mathematics, in ONE sitting?
eligibility.no: Two sittings did not qualify in 2025/26. Consider NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS or other awards.

eligibility.q: Did you score 200 or more in UTME?
eligibility.no: You cannot apply this year. Other awards (e.g. Nigerian Scholarship Awards) may use different rules.

eligibility.q: Are you 18-25 years old at the time of applying?
eligibility.no: If you are 17, check whether you will be 18 by the next opening; if over 25, look at other undergraduate awards.

eligibility.q: Are you free of any other scholarship, bursary or grant, and not a relative of NLNG staff?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible. Choose one scholarship.

steps.title: Check you meet every rule
steps.why: Many applicants fail the first screen on one small rule, like a two-sitting O'Level or a private university.
do: Open the NLNG UGSS page on the official application portal and read the eligibility list.
Tick each rule only if you have the document to prove it.
Confirm your university is federal or state, not private.
Check your age on your birth certificate - you must be 18-25 when you apply.
tips: Rules are checked against documents, so one-sitting results and correct dates matter.
avoid: Applying with two sittings 'just to try'.
check: I meet every rule and have proof.

steps.title: Understand how NLNG selects
steps.why: There is no essay. Your documents get you to the test and the test decides most of the result.
do: Note the stages: document review, online proctored selection test for the shortlisted, extra mandatory documents, award.
Plan to spend most of your preparation on aptitude practice.
Write your backup list: NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS (100 and 200 level), Agbami (medicine/engineering), state scholarships.
tips: NLNG says to follow its newspaper notices and social media for updates.
avoid: Thinking a high UTME score alone wins.
check: I know the stages and have backups.

steps.title: Set reminders for the November-December window
steps.why: The 2025/26 window was only about three and a half weeks long.
do: Put a reminder for early November to check the NLNG portal and nigerialng.com.
Follow NLNG's official social media pages.
Set a goal to submit within the first week the portal opens.
tips: Use only the official smapply.io portal linked from NLNG - not copies on blogs.
check: I have reminders set and know the real portal address.

steps.title: Create an email you will check and a portal account
steps.why: Test invitations come by email. A lost password or full inbox can cost you the award.
do: Create or choose a personal email you check daily, with a clear name.
When the portal opens, register on the NLNG application portal and confirm your email.
Save your login details somewhere safe.
Add the portal domain to your contacts so emails do not go to spam.
tips: Use your own phone number, not a parent's, so you get SMS alerts.
avoid: Creating two accounts - one applicant, one application.
check: I can log in and receive portal emails.

steps.title: Get your O'Level and JAMB documents
steps.why: These are the core proof of eligibility.
do: Get a copy of your WAEC/NECO/SSCE result or certificate (one sitting).
Print your UTME result slip from the JAMB portal.
Print your JAMB admission letter from the JAMB portal (CAPS).
Scan each one clearly as PDF or JPG.
tips: If your WAEC certificate is not out yet, keep the printed result and checker PIN ready.
check: I have clear scans of O'Level, UTME result and JAMB admission letter.

steps.title: Get your LGA letter, birth certificate and photo
steps.why: These confirm your identity, age and state of origin.
do: Visit your Local Government secretariat and request an LGA identification letter.
Find your birth certificate or apply for one through the National Population Commission.
Take a recent passport photograph without glasses.
Check your name is spelled the same on every document; if not, swear an affidavit.
tips: Ask for two original LGA letters - you may need one later.
avoid: A photo with glasses - the 2025/26 rules said no glasses.
check: I have LGA letter, birth certificate and a no-glasses photo scanned.

steps.title: Tell your department you are applying
steps.why: NLNG did not ask for reference letters in 2025/26, but winners must send extra mandatory documents after the test, which can include proof of studentship.
do: Get your student ID card or matriculation number ready.
Tell your course adviser you are applying and may need a letter confirming you are a full-time student.
Note the department office hours so you can get a stamped letter quickly if asked.
tips: Ask early - department offices close for holidays in December.
avoid: Waiting until NLNG gives you a short deadline.
check: I know who can confirm my studentship quickly.

steps.title: Write a short honest profile (no essay required)
steps.why: The 2025/26 form had no essay, but some fields ask for personal information. Clear answers avoid mistakes.
do: Write down your full names, date of birth, state, LGA, university, course and matriculation number exactly as on your documents.
Prepare your parents' or guardian's contact details.
Keep this sheet beside you while filling the form.
tips: Copy names exactly as on your JAMB admission letter.
avoid: Typing from memory and mixing up the order of names.
check: My details sheet matches my documents.

steps.title: Fill the form and upload documents
do: Log in to the NLNG portal and start the UGSS application.
Fill every required field from your details sheet.
Upload photo, O'Level, UTME result, JAMB admission letter, LGA letter and birth certificate.
Open each upload to check it is the right file.
tips: Use a laptop and good internet; save as you go.
avoid: Leaving optional-looking fields empty if they apply to you.

steps.title: Proofread, submit and save proof
steps.why: False or wrong details disqualify you, and portals slow down before the deadline.
do: Read every field aloud and compare with your documents.
Submit at least a week before the closing date.
Screenshot the submitted status and save the confirmation email.
tips: Ask a friend to check your scans and spelling.
check: My application shows submitted and I have proof.

steps.title: Practise for the online proctored test
steps.time: 10-20 hours over two to three weeks
steps.why: The proctored computer-based test is the main filter. Practice makes a big difference.
do: Practise verbal reasoning (comprehension, word meaning) and numerical reasoning (percentages, ratios, data tables) daily.
Do timed practice sets on a computer, not on paper.
Revise basic current affairs about Nigeria and the energy sector.
Read every instruction in the test invitation email, including software or browser requirements.
tips: Time yourself: aim to answer each question in under a minute.
avoid: Buying 'past questions' from unknown sellers - formats change.
check: I have done at least five timed practice sets.

steps.title: Set up for test day
steps.why: Online proctoring watches your camera and screen. A technical failure can end your test.
do: Get a laptop with a working webcam and microphone.
Arrange stable internet and backup power for the full test time.
Choose a quiet, well-lit room with nobody else in it and a clear desk.
Do any system check the invitation asks for, a day before.
Log in 30 minutes early with your ID ready.
tips: If you lack a laptop, arrange a quiet borrowed one in advance and test it.
avoid: Taking the test in a busy cafe or with your phone in reach.
check: My device passes the system check and I have backup power.

steps.title: Submit final documents and accept the award
steps.why: Only candidates who submit all extra mandatory documents after the test are awarded.
do: Watch your email and SMS after the test.
Submit any extra documents requested before the stated deadline.
Follow instructions to accept the award and give your bank details through the official process only.
Keep your grades up - continuing support depends on staying in good standing.
tips: Reply quickly; deadlines after the test can be short.
avoid: Sharing bank details with anyone outside the official NLNG process.
check: I have received and accepted a written award.
